text: The tripwire blocked a command this session had written, and the session recorded it as a false positive and built a rule to allow the shape — a quoted-delimiter heredoc body treated as data the shell never runs. The blocked command was 'bash <<SH', whose body bash executes, so the block had been correct and the rule shipped five silent passes: the premise, plus four delimiter spellings two reviewers reproduced against the built binary. What the diagnosis skipped was reading the blocked command's own head. Whether a heredoc body is a document or a script is the receiving program's to decide, and no rule reading the command line can tell them apart, so the body stays in the scan and a document that quotes a flag at line start keeps false-blocking.
source: release review of f7ee0c3..HEAD, 2026-09-15; two independent reviewers, five silent passes reproduced
